Let's say that US Treasury debt paying 2% interest. If the US adopts negative interest rates (as Japan and some Euro countries have done) of say -4%, then wouldn't the gov end up paying people who own Treasuries 98 cents on the dollar? In essence defaulting? Like the article says?

Not a default. They will continue paying the 2% coupon on all existing debt. The -4% coupon will only be applied to new debt issuances, however, if the market still demands a positive return on treasuries, then the notes will be issued at a very steep discount to face value. So even though the notes technically pay negative, the lenders could potentially still make money.

The default will occur when the Treasury misses a payment, pays late, or does not pay in full.

More realistically, the Treasury will make good on its payments by printing money and sacrificing the dollar's value and reserve currency status. So no technical default, but a similar or worse result.
